setOperations.title: Set Operations
setOperations.hint: click a number to see why, or press start to check the regions one by one

union.rule: A\cup B=\{x \mid x \in A \text{ or } x \in B\}

intersection.meaning: intersection: in $A$ and in $B$ at once
intersection.rule: A\cap B=\{x \mid x \in A \text{ and } x \in B\}

symmetric.meaning: symmetric difference: in $A$ or in $B$, but not both

complementOfUnion.meaning: complement of the union: not in $A$ and not in $B$

cartesianProduct.title: Cartesian Product
cartesianProduct.hint: click a point or a member on an axis, or press start to pair them one by one

rule.axes: first member from ${{first}}$ (horizontal axis), second member from ${{second}}$ (vertical axis).

count.each: each member of ${{first}}$ has ${{rows}}$ pairs, and ${{first}}$ has ${{columns}}$ members.

order.same: ${{pair}}$ stays the same when swapped, so it is in both, because ${{x}}\in {{first}}$ and ${{x}}\in {{second}}$.
order.conclusion: so ${{product}}\neq {{swappedProduct}}$, even though they have the same number of members: ${{size}}={{size}}$.

reasons.columnDone: ${{x}}$ is now paired with every member of ${{second}}$.
reasons.point: ${{pair}}$: ${{x}}\in {{first}}$ is read on the horizontal axis, ${{y}}\in {{second}}$ on the vertical axis. The point sits where those two dashed lines meet.
reasons.column: ${{x}}$ is paired with every member of ${{second}}$: ${{pairs}}$. That is ${{count}}$ pairs, one column.
reasons.row: ${{y}}$ is the second member in ${{count}}$ pairs: ${{pairs}}$. One row.
reasons.final: ${{product}}$: every member of ${{first}}$ is paired with every member of ${{second}}$. Each pair is one point.

operationLimits.title: Limits of Operations
operationLimits.hint: click a table cell, or play to work through it one by one

closed.rule: ${{set}}$ is closed under {{operation}} if ${{expression}}\in {{set}}$ for every $a,b\in {{set}}$.
closed.ruleNonzero: ${{set}}$ is closed under {{operation}} if ${{expression}}\in {{set}}$ for every $a,b\in {{set}}$ with $b\neq 0$.
closed.yesReason: the table only holds examples. The reason: {{reason}}

reasons.sum: the sum of two {{plural}} is always {{singular}}.
reasons.difference: the difference of two {{plural}} is always {{singular}}.
reasons.product: the product of two {{plural}} is always {{singular}}.
reasons.quotient: $\tfrac{p}{q}\div\tfrac{r}{s}=\tfrac{p\times s}{q\times r}$ with $r\neq 0$: the numerator and denominator stay integers, so the result is rational.

closed.skipped: {{count}} cells divide by $0$ and are skipped.

summary.footnote: yes = closed. For $\div$, the divisor is $\neq 0$.

reasons.zero: the result is $0$, which first appears in $\mathbb{C}_a$
reasons.negative: the result is a negative integer, which first appears in $\mathbb{Z}$
reasons.fraction: the result is a fraction, which first appears in $\mathbb{Q}$
reasons.undefined: ${{dividend}}\div 0$: division by $0$ is undefined, so this cell is skipped.
reasons.final: this table works out ${{expression}}$ for five sample members of ${{set}}$. Highlighted results are $\in {{set}}$, results circled in red are $\notin {{set}}$.
